points.quote: Using an AI agent within Learn or any other University learning or assessment platform which requires you to log in is not permitted.
points.gist: Using an AI agent inside Learn or any other login-required learning or assessment platform is not permitted.

points.quote: Sharing your login details with an agent or agentic browser is a breach of the University Computing Acceptable Use Policy. This will result in your access to University digital services being removed and disciplinary action being taken against you.
points.gist: Sharing login details with an agent or agentic browser breaches the Acceptable Use Policy and leads to removed access and disciplinary action.

points.quote: Using an AI translator to convert assessed work to English before submission: English is the language of teaching and assessment at Edinburgh – machine translation is treated as false authorship and is not acceptable.
points.anchor: Unacceptable uses of generative AI for assessment
points.gist: Using an AI translator to convert assessed work to English before submission is treated as false authorship and is not acceptable.

points.quote: Submitting an assessment which includes AI-generated mathematical formulae or reasoning, or computer code, without acknowledgment.
points.anchor: Unacceptable uses of generative AI for assessment
points.gist: Submitting an assessment with AI-generated formulae, reasoning or code without acknowledgment is not acceptable and constitutes misconduct.

points.quote: Citing and referencing AI-found sources without reading and verifying them.
points.anchor: Unacceptable uses of generative AI for assessment
points.gist: Citing and referencing AI-found sources without reading and verifying them is not acceptable.

points.quote: The University does not ban the use of AI, though its use will be restricted for much of your assessed work.
points.anchor: Using generative AI in your studies: guidelines for students
points.gist: The University does not ban AI, but its use will be restricted for much of your assessed work.

points.quote: You must always check your course level guidance.
points.anchor: Using generative AI in your studies: guidelines for students
points.gist: You must always check your course level guidance.

points.quote: As a result, you must not use third-party AI-based translation apps in class.
points.anchor: Use of live translation apps in class
points.gist: You must not use third-party AI-based translation apps in class.

points.quote: You should only use the University’s generative AI service – ELM – to do this as it has in-built privacy protections.
points.anchor: Use of live translation apps in class
points.gist: For translation outside class to understand notes, you should only use the University's generative AI service, ELM, which has in-built privacy protections.

points.quote: You should include a brief acknowledgment at the end of your piece of work, for example:
points.gist: If you use generative AI for permitted aspects of an assessment, you should include a brief acknowledgment at the end of your work.

points.quote: If you use content generated by AI within your work, for example an AI-generated image or text from an AI chatbot, you will need to reference it.
points.anchor: Citing your use of generative AI
points.gist: AI-generated content used in your work must be referenced with an in-text citation or footnote and a reference-list entry.

points.quote: You will be held accountable for these errors and biases if you include them in assessed work.
points.gist: You will be held accountable for AI errors and biases that you include in assessed work.

points.quote: In ELM your data is secure – it will not be retained by third party services to train their models or for any other purpose.
points.anchor: Using the University’s own generative AI platform (ELM)
points.gist: In ELM your data is secure and will not be retained by third party services to train their models or for any other purpose.

points.quote: Those on professionally accredited programmes may be referred for fitness to practice concerns if found to engage in academic misconduct.
points.anchor: Unacceptable uses of generative AI for assessment
points.gist: Students on professionally accredited programmes found to engage in academic misconduct may be referred for fitness to practice concerns.

points.quote: If you are concerned about this, consider using the locally-hosted instance of Llama in ELM (see above).
points.anchor: Environmental and social impact of generative AI
points.gist: If you are concerned about environmental impact, consider using the locally-hosted instance of Llama in ELM.

points.quote: If you routinely use generative AI for breaking down and summarising long texts, for example, you will not be developing your own critical skills in the analysis of complex documents.
points.gist: Routinely using generative AI to break down and summarise long texts means you will not be developing your own critical analysis skills.
